title: Our Story | R&SVP – Hio Ridge, Bridgton, Maine
description: Meet Susan and Richard Voth, the owners of R&SVP in Bridgton, Maine. Their wedding barn holds original boards and windows saved from the family home.
heading: We kept the house windows. *They're in the barn now.*
lede: When Richard suggested replacing the house windows, Susan wanted to put the old ones in the barn. That decision became part of a much bigger project. We're Susan and Richard Voth. We restored this barn for weddings and events on the farm Susan's family has owned since 1941.
hero_alt: Susan and Richard Voth, smiling, at the barn door

sections.heading: Summers on the family farm
body: Susan's father and his brother spent summers here helping their grandfather, Howard Burnham. Howard and Rosa, Susan's great grandparents, bought the farm in 1941.
Susan's grandmother, Phyllis Shackley, later spent 25 retirement years here. Susan's father followed with 25 years of his own. Susan is now the fourth generation to own the farm.
sections.alt: A black and white portrait of Rosa and Howard Burnham

sections.heading: We came back to work on the house.
body: We returned in October 2020 after Susan retired. The barn was still serving as a garage. As we worked on the house, we began finding ways to use its old materials in the barn.

A friend suggested turning the property into a place for overnight guests. We decided to host events. We named the venue R&SVP for Richard and Susan Voth Properties. Hio Ridge is the name of our road.
sections.alt: The barn in 2020: dark weathered boards, a sagging roofline, grass in front

sections.heading: We made ceremony benches from the old floorboards.
body: We made ceremony benches from the barn's old floorboards. We used its original exterior boards to line the walls inside, and kept the old house windows for the barn.

Tim Brown and his team at Brown Solutions restored the building. Greg Bouley of River's Edge Landscaping used stones from beneath it for the planters and seating circle. You can see their work as you walk through the barn and grounds.
sections.alt: The ell and barn during renovation, new boards on the ell, the old barn beside it

sections.heading: Music in the barn, neighbors at the tables
body: The High Street Jazz Band played at our open house. Since then, we've welcomed guests for cardmaking and tours of the farm.
We want the barn to serve our community, too. We've pledged to donate use of the venue for one charitable event each year. When you hold an event here, we're on site.
sections.alt: A stone planter filled with perennials, the field behind

credits_heading: The people who helped us restore it

closing.heading: Meet us at the barn.
closing.body: Susan can show you through the barn and hear what you have in mind for your wedding or event. Contact her to schedule a tour.
